investor_summary:
## Key Drivers

• **Automobile exports** — Passenger vehicle exports fell 17% in August, pressuring the automobile sector. With this sector representing a meaningful part of the portfolio, the broad weakness was a drag on the fund.

• **Nationwide bank strike** — The September 11 bank strike disrupted banking services and hurt sentiment for lenders, notably ICICI Bank and State Bank of India. SBI also faced margin concerns from rising FCNR(B) deposit hedging costs, adding to the negative pressure on bank holdings.

• **US tariff threat on India** — The US House advanced a bill for 100% tariffs on India, raising trade-war fears and weighing on export-linked large caps such as Reliance Industries. This contributed to the fund's decline.

• **HDFC Bank** — The stock rose as its CEO appointment process advanced and brokerages stayed bullish; Macquarie highlighted upside and a CEO candidate as a potential re-rating catalyst. As the fund's largest holding, this was a significant positive offset.

• **Infosys** — Infosys and other IT names gained after Anthropic's CEO called for slower AI development, which lifted sentiment toward the sector. Infosys ADRs also surged, helping this holding provide a positive offset.

## Overall Summary

The fund declined this week, mainly because automobile exports weakened, the September 11 bank strike pressured major lenders, and US tariff threats weighed on Reliance Industries. These drags were partially offset by HDFC Bank's CEO-related re-rating and Infosys's AI-sentiment-driven gain. The takeaway is that broad sector and policy headlines drove the week, with large holdings providing some support but not enough to overcome the negative pressure.
